title: Low-resolution Metropolis Monte Carlo survey
action: Run low-resolution Metropolis simulations of the BA Hamiltonian on 3D cubic lattices (L=6,7,8,9,10,12) for J2=0.5,0.7,0.8,0.9,1.0,1.2 over a wide temperature range to locate approximate transition regions. Use single-spin-flip updates, adjust angle steps for ~50% acceptance, 100k MCS equilibration, 200k MCS data collection per temperature.

title: High-resolution multihistogram Monte Carlo simulations
action: For each J2 and lattice size L=6,8,10,12, perform multiple independent Metropolis simulations at several temperatures around each transition. Equilibrate 5e5 MCS, collect 1e6 MCS data per temperature, discard 10-20 sweeps between measurements. Save energy histograms for each temperature.

title: Histogram reweighting and extraction of size-dependent quantities
action: Combine histograms via Ferrenberg-Swendsen multihistogram algorithm to obtain specific heat C(T) and Binder cumulant U_L(T) curves. Extract C_max(L), U_min(L), effective T_c(L) for each transition feature.

title: Finite-size scaling and phase-diagram assembly
action: For each J2, fit C_max(L), U_min(L), T_c(L) to scaling laws to classify order and extract bulk Tc. Compile results into phase_diagram.csv. For J2<0.9 two rows (I-H and H-L) with I-H at higher Tc; for J2>=0.9 one row (I-L).
description: Phase diagram: for each J2, the transition(s), their infinite-size critical temperatures in units of J1, and order (first or second). The critical end point is the I-L transition at J2=0.9.
output_schema: CSV with columns: J2 (float), transition (string, one of 'I-H', 'H-L', 'I-L'), Tc (float, transition temperature in units of J1), order (string, 'second' or 'first'). For J2<0.9, two rows (I-H and H-L) with I-H at higher Tc. For J2>=0.9, one row (I-L).
